To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have set up a system to study gene expression in tumor cells that allows a medium-scale survey of expression levels and that we have validated this system on a set of 120 genes in three mammary carcinoma cells.

a medium-scale expression survey can be carried out with good-quality data, and can be used to identify genes that may be involved in the development of cancer, and that the method can be applied to tumor samples.
we have established a medium-scale, high-density, flexible system for the study of gene expression in cancer cells and have validated it with a set of six cell lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of macroarrays for the analysis of gene expression on the medium scale.
the development of a system for the study of expression levels in human tumors and the use of this system in the analysis of a set of genes implicated in growth and differentiation.
developing a medium-scale, quantitative, flexible, and relatively low-cost system to study gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method is robust, flexible, and can be used for a wide variety of applications.

this system, which is based on the use of a set of 120 genes on Nylon macroarrays and radioactive detection, is a valid, flexible and relatively inexpensive tool for expression profiling of tumor samples.
the method described is suitable for the study of gene expression at medium scale and for the identification of potential targets for the development of new therapies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the IMAGE resource can be used to assemble medium-scale arrays, and the results obtained can be used to validate and refine the expression patterns of a number of genes, including some that have not been previously studied.

a medium-scale gene expression scanning procedure, based on the IMAGE resource and a simple macroarray technology, can be a useful approach for the analysis of tumor gene expression, and for the identification of new markers of cancer.
a medium-scale gene expression study is feasible with the IMAGE collection, provided that certain conditions are respected, and that the resulting data can be useful for the study of carcinogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a flexible, medium-scale approach to the study of gene expression can provide valuable information in a cost-effective manner, with the potential of being applied to a variety of problems.
the use of this approach in the context of clinical investigations requires a high level of quality control.
it is possible to obtain reliable, quantitative data on the expression levels of large sets of genes in human tumor samples, and to use them to identify new targets of carcinogenesis.
